maria: Heads-up — noticed a p95 regression on /chat-stream (tier B routes) after the small-batch kernel switchover. p95 jumped ~55ms over baseline around 18:12 UTC.
kevin: ugh. same servers as the canary? any KV hit-rate change?
maria: yes canary landed on 18:09. KV hit-rate for those routes dropped from ~72% -> ~48% in the window. stack trace/short logs below.
perf-bot: alert: p95 latency > SLO for route=/chat-stream tier=B at 2026-03-15T18:12:07Z. Cats: kernel-choice, kv-misses, small-batches
sam: can you paste the flamegraph output or a quick profile snippet?
maria: flamegraph: main hotspots were: 1) decoding kernel path for small-batch (20-40 tokens) 2) KV lookup loop when prefix==large (higher miss cost) 3) queue wake path overhead. short sample:
```
# profile sample (aggregated 30s)
decode_kernel_small_batch_ms: 34.1
kv_lookup_ms_per_req: 12.4
queue_lock_wait_ms: 3.6
other: 5.2
p95_total_ms: 121.7
```
nisha: sounds like adverse interaction: new kernel reduced compute cost for some cases but increases prep/packing overhead and changes batching dynamics -> smaller batches -> worse KV amortization.
ethan: agree. small batches mean less prefix sharing -> KV cache less effective -> miss amplification.
kevin: practical question: do we fix kernel preferences or tune batching heuristics (token budgets / queue policy) so we keep kernel gains where they help but avoid chopping up requests?
maria: proposed quick experiment:
1) change queue policy to size-weighted-FIFO (prefer grouping by expected tokens, not only arrival order)
2) add route-tier token_budget targets (dynamic): compute token_budget = max(min_budget, floor(latency_budget / avg_token_ms)) per tier
3) prefer prefetch+async KV for routes with long prefixes (non-blocking) to reduce miss tail
config snippet to try (canary 5%):
```
{
  "batcher": {
    "queue_policy": "size_weighted_fifo",
    "token_budget_by_tier": {
      "gold": 120,
      "silver": 64,
      "bronze": 24
    },
    "min_budget": 8,
    "kernel_preference": ["fast_small_batch_kernel","int8_kernel","fallback_default"],
    "kv_prefetch_async": true
  }
}
```
sam: I like it. We should also instrument per-route average token_ms so the dynamic calc is observable. Add metric: route.token_ms_ema and route.target_budget.
nisha: also add an experiment to bump prefix cache TTL for these routes (short-term) to see whether KV hit dilution is the real culprit.
ethan: canary steps? I can run deploy. Suggest 5% traffic to the canary pool, 30m ramp, evaluate p95 and kv-hit per-route. rollback if p95 > baseline+40ms.
kevin: add a kernel hedging policy: if batch size < 4 use kernel A, else kernel B. That keeps small request latency low but avoids splitting medium batches.
maria: agreed. final plan:
- canary config as above + kernel hedging
- metrics: p95, p99, route.token_ms_ema, kv_hit_rate, avg_batch_size, batch_split_rate
- rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% if p95 <= baseline+20ms and kv_hit_rate recovers to >65%
- rollback triggers: p95 > baseline+40ms or kv_hit_rate <50% sustained 10m
ethan: /deploy batcher-config canary --route /chat-stream --percent 5 --config ./canary-batcher.json
maria: I'll add dashboards and alert rules. tagging @kevin @nisha for followups. any other blockers?
sam: need a quick perf test harness to replay traffic with preserved prefix distributions. I'll spin that up and post results in 30m.
kevin: Also add a short-lived synthetic test that forces high prefix-sharing to estimate best-case kv_hit amortization.
nisha: +1. also document the kernel hedging thresholds in the config so SRE can tune after.
maria: ok capturing action items:
- ethan: run canary deploy + monitor (18:40 UTC)
- sam: replay harness results (start 18:45 UTC)
- nisha: TTL tweak experiment and docs
- kevin: add synthetic prefix-sharing test
- maria: dashboards/alerts + canary criteria
